title: Local CMS for Astro — Avocado
description: Edit Astro content collections, images, references, and Markdown in a local CMS. Keep project files canonical and deploy without an Avocado runtime.
headline: Your content doesn't need a second source of truth.
intro: Avocado reads your Astro content collections and gives them a visual editing surface while keeping the actual project files canonical. No hosted content database required. No Avocado runtime required on the finished website.

sections.title: The schema becomes the interface.
body: Avocado evaluates the project's own Astro content configuration and uses it to understand your collections.
Text. Numbers. Dates. Images. References. Markdown. Validation. The content editor can work with the types your project already defines.
The project defines the model. Avocado provides the interface.
sections.code:
src/content.config.ts  → Collection schemas
src/content/           → Content entries
src/assets/            → Related images

sections.title: Edit content without forgetting that it is code.
body: Browse collections. Choose an entry. Edit structured fields. Write Markdown content. Follow references. See backlinks. Validate the result. Save it back into the project.
Content remains versionable through Git like the rest of the website.

sections.title: References become visible.
body: Content relationships are difficult when they exist only as IDs and filenames. Avocado derives an index that can connect entries, references, backlinks, page usage, and related assets.
The index is disposable. Your files are not.
Delete the index and rebuild it. Your content remains the same.

sections.title: Know before you delete.
body: A referenced entry should not disappear silently. A used asset should not be removed without context.
Avocado can use its derived index to surface references and delete guards before destructive content operations.

sections.title: Assets belong beside the content that uses them.
body: Upload. Preview. Organize. Select assets from content fields. Inspect content backlinks before removing referenced files.

items.title: src/assets
items.body: Files processed through Astro's asset pipeline.

items.title: public
items.body: Files copied directly into the final site.

sections.title: Content without a SaaS dependency.
body: Your CMS can be part of the development environment without becoming part of the production infrastructure.
Build with Avocado. Commit with Git. Deploy through your existing workflow. Run the finished website without Avocado.

sections.title: Built around your Astro schema.
body: Full collection schema introspection currently depends on the Astro and Zod versions supported by Avocado's current CMS implementation.
For the current pre-alpha, Astro 6+ is the primary target for full CMS schema introspection.
